reading.body:
The Independent Community Bankers of America filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports naming AI, making it one of the more active banking trade groups on the issue.

The filings name 22 lobbyists, but the counts cluster tightly: 11 lobbyists appear on all 8 filings, three on 6, three on 4, and three on 2 or fewer. That pattern suggests a core team carries the AI portfolio while others are named incidentally across a broader registration. Two bills are named, HR 2152 and S 2296, both from 2025 or later.

For AI specifically, this is a signal about who is at the table when financial-sector AI rules get written. Community banks are the institutions most exposed to AI-driven credit scoring and fraud detection, and their trade group is registering AI as a lobbying subject rather than leaving it to the largest banks. The bills named are the concrete legislative hooks, though the data does not say what position the ICBA took on either.

What the data does not cover: the substance of any filing, the amounts spent, which agencies were contacted, or whether the AI mentions are central or incidental to each report. A firm that files for a client reports that it lobbied on an issue, not the position it argued. Nothing here connects to compute, data centers, or power.

summary: INDEPENDENT COMMUNITY BANKERS OF AMERICA filed 8 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 19194.
